title: Profile and Clean the Data

header.html: Evaluate data, including data statistics and column properties; Resolve inconsistencies, unexpected or null values, and data quality issues; Resolve data import errors
the official PL-300 study guide (skills measured as of April 20, 2026)

toc.title: Resolve inconsistencies, nulls and quality issues

html:
1Profile the data

The data profiling tools of the Power Query Editor show the quality of each column before you load it. Turn them on in the View tab, in the Data preview group.

Tool What it shows
Column quality The percent of Valid, Error and Empty values in each column
Column distribution A bar chart of how often values occur, with the counts of distinct and unique values
Column profile Statistics for the selected column and a value distribution chart

By default the tools profile only the first 1,000 rows. To profile everything, choose Column profiling based on entire data set in the lower-left status bar. A bad value in row 50,000 stays invisible until you switch.

Exam tip

. Profiling covers only the first 1,000 rows by default. Switch to Column profiling based on entire data set before you trust a 0% error figure.

2Statistics and column properties

The Column profile pane lists statistics that answer the first cleaning questions.

Statistic What it tells you
Count, Error, Empty How many rows, how many errors, how many blanks
Distinct The number of different values, each counted once
Unique The number of values that occur exactly once
Minimum, maximum, average The range and center of a number column

On a key column, distinct and unique should both equal the row count. If distinct is lower, the key has duplicates. A spike in the distribution chart or an odd minimum, such as a negative quantity, points to unexpected values.

Column properties you check while evaluating data: the column name, the data type icon in the header (the icon "ABC 123" means Any, so no type is set) and the share of Empty values. After the data loads, the Column tools in Data view show the name, data type, format, data category and summarization. Module 5 covers them.

A blank-looking cell can be a null or an empty string. They are different values, so a command that targets one can miss the other.

Exam tip

. Distinct counts every different value once; unique counts only values that occur exactly once. On a key column both should equal the row count.

3Resolve inconsistencies, nulls and quality issues

Most cleaning commands are on the Transform tab. Remove Rows and Keep Rows are on the Home tab.

Problem Command
Placeholder or misspelled values Replace Values
Cells that show Error Remove Errors deletes those rows; Replace Errors keeps the rows and puts in a value
A value shown once, with nulls below or above it Fill Down or Fill Up
Extra spaces and invisible characters Trim removes leading and trailing spaces; Clean removes non-printable characters
Mixed capitalization lowercase, UPPERCASE or Capitalize Each Word
Repeated rows Remove Duplicates on the selected columns
Rows you do not need Remove Rows: top, bottom, alternate, blank rows, errors

Three details decide many questions. Fill Down fills null cells with the value from the row above, but it skips empty strings, so replace empty strings with null first. Remove Duplicates is case-sensitive and sees a trailing space as a difference, so trim and fix the case first. Remove Errors loses rows, while Replace Errors keeps them.

For null values choose one action on purpose: keep the null, replace it with a default such as "Unknown", or fill it from neighboring rows. A null is not a zero: averages skip nulls, so replacing nulls with 0 changes the average.

let
    Source = Customer,
    Trimmed = Table.TransformColumns(Source, {{"Name", Text.Trim}}),
    Cleaned = Table.TransformColumns(Trimmed, {{"Name", Text.Clean}}),
    Proper = Table.TransformColumns(Cleaned, {{"Name", Text.Proper}}),
    Unique = Table.Distinct(Proper, {"CustomerID"})
in
    Unique
Exam tip

. Remove Errors deletes the rows; Replace Errors keeps them and substitutes a value. Use Replace Errors when the business wants every row.

Exam tip

. Fill Down fills only null cells, and Remove Duplicates is case-sensitive. Replace empty strings with null before Fill Down, and trim before removing duplicates.

4Resolve data import errors

An error in the Applied Steps pane or in a cell tells you which step failed. For a cell error, select the cell without clicking the word Error, and the details appear below the grid. Keep Errors on the Home tab shows only the error rows.

Error Typical message Fix
Type conversion DataFormat.Error: We couldn't convert to Number Find the bad values, then Replace Values or Replace Errors, or use the right locale
Column not found Expression.Error: The column 'X' of the table wasn't found The source column was renamed: edit the step in Applied Steps to the new name
Missing file DataSource.Error: Could not find file Data source settings, then Change Source; keep the path in a parameter
Credentials A prompt or an access error Edit Permissions; in the service the model owner edits credentials
Privacy level A firewall error that mentions privacy levels Set the privacy levels of the combined sources in Data source settings

Some errors appear only after refresh. The editor works from a sample, so rows or new values that break a step may show up only on a full load. Profile the entire data set, handle errors with Remove Errors or Replace Errors, and use Refresh Preview to test.

In the service the owner gets a failure email, and the schedule is disabled after four consecutive failures.

let
    Source = Sales,
    Fixed = Table.ReplaceErrorValues(Source, {{"Amount", 0}}),
    Removed = Table.RemoveRowsWithErrors(Fixed, {"Quantity"})
in
    Removed
Exam tip

. A "column not found" error after a source rename is fixed in Applied Steps, in the step that uses the old name. Do not change the model or the credentials.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A table has millions of rows. Column quality shows 0% errors in the editor, but the load fails with conversion errors. What most likely explains this?

  • AColumn quality profiled only the first 1,000 rows by default
  • BColumn distribution hides error values from the preview
  • CColumn profile is available only after the data is loaded
  • DColumn quality counts only the rows that contain nulls
Show the answer

Answer: A. Profiling uses the first 1,000 rows unless you switch to the entire data set.

S2A Region column shows a value only on the first row of each group, and the rows below are null. Which transformation fills every row with its region?

  • AFill Up on the Region column
  • BRemove Errors on the Region column
  • CReplace Errors on the Region column
  • DFill Down on the Region column
Show the answer

Answer: D. Fill Down copies the value from above into the null cells below it.

S3After a Change Type step, some Quantity cells show Error because the source holds the text n/a. The business wants every row kept, with zero in those cells. What should you use?

  • ARemove Errors, which deletes the rows with errors
  • BKeep Errors, which keeps only the rows with errors
  • CFill Down, which copies the last good value down
  • DReplace Errors, with 0 as the replacement value
Show the answer

Answer: D. Replace Errors keeps the rows and substitutes the value you choose.

S4A refresh fails with the message that the column OrderDt of the table wasn't found, because the source team renamed it. Where do you fix the query?

  • AIn Data source settings, by choosing Clear Permissions
  • BIn Applied Steps, by editing the step that uses the old name
  • CIn Model view, by renaming the column in the Properties pane
  • DIn the service, by editing the credentials of the model
Show the answer

Answer: B. The step that references the old name must be edited to use the new column name.

S5A customer list holds one person as "ann lee" and as "Ann Lee " with a trailing space, and Remove Duplicates keeps both. What should you do before removing duplicates?

  • AApply Trim, then Capitalize Each Word to the column
  • BApply Change Type, then Replace Errors to the column
  • CApply Fill Down, then Keep Errors to the column
  • DApply Clean, then Remove Errors to the column
Show the answer

Answer: A. Remove Duplicates is case-sensitive and sees spaces, so trimming and fixing the case makes the two values equal.

S6A scheduled refresh fails because the source password changed, and another user owns the semantic model. What must you do to edit its credentials?

  • AClear the permissions in Power BI Desktop
  • BTake over the semantic model in its settings
  • CChange the page settings of the report
  • DShare the model with the Reshare permission
Show the answer

Answer: B. Only the owner edits credentials, so you take over the model first.

5.2 Recall questions

R1How many rows do the profiling tools use by default?

Show the answer

The first 1,000 rows.

R2How do you profile the entire data set?

Show the answer

Choose Column profiling based on entire data set in the lower-left status bar.

R3Which command keeps the rows and replaces error cells with a value?

Show the answer

Replace Errors.

R4What does Fill Down fill?

Show the answer

Null cells, with the value from the row above.

R5Which two commands remove extra spaces and non-printable characters?

Show the answer

Trim and Clean.

R6Where do you look first for the step that fails?

Show the answer

The Applied Steps pane and the details of the error cell.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Profiling tools View tab, Data preview: Column quality, Column distribution, Column profile
Default scope first 1,000 rows; switch to the entire data set in the lower-left status bar
Statistics distinct is each different value once; unique is values that occur exactly once
Errors Remove Errors deletes rows; Replace Errors keeps rows; Keep Errors shows only error rows
Cleaning Replace Values, Fill Down and Fill Up (nulls only), Trim, Clean, Capitalize Each Word, Remove Duplicates (case-sensitive)
Nulls keep, replace with a default or fill; null is not zero
Import errors type conversion, column not found (edit the step), missing file (Change Source), credentials, privacy level, errors only after refresh
